questions.q: What are the three parts of an Azure Monitor alert rule?
options: Signal, condition, and action group
Workspace, table, and query
Resource, region, and subscription
Metric, log, and trace
questions.explain: An alert rule combines a signal (the data source), a condition (the threshold logic), and an action group (what fires when the condition is met).

questions.q: Why is an Action Group a separate, reusable Azure resource instead of being defined inside each alert rule?
options: Because Azure requires every resource to be billed separately
So that changing an escalation policy means updating one action group instead of every alert rule that uses it
Because action groups can only be used once
Because alert rules cannot contain any configuration themselves
questions.explain: Action groups are standalone resources attachable to many alert rules, so an operational change (like a new on-call webhook) only has to be made in one place.

questions.q: What does an alert rule's severity level (Sev 0–4) control?
options: Whether the alert rule fires at all
How the alert is sorted and presented in the Alerts list, for triage
The price of running the alert rule
How many action groups can be attached
questions.explain: Severity doesn't affect whether a condition triggers the alert — it shapes how alerts are triaged and sorted, so critical issues stand out from low-priority ones.

questions.q: A condition is defined as 'average response time over 2000ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute periods.' What part of the alert rule is this?
options: The action group
The signal
The condition — the threshold logic applied to the signal
The severity
questions.explain: This threshold logic is the condition. The signal would be the metric itself (e.g., AverageResponseTime); the condition is the rule applied to that signal's values.

questions.q: Which of these could be configured as actions inside a single Action Group?
options: Only email notifications — one action type per group
Email, SMS, webhook, Azure Function, Logic App, and runbook actions together
Only Azure Functions
Action groups cannot contain any notification actions
questions.explain: An action group can bundle multiple action types together — for example, paging on-call via SMS and posting to a Teams channel via webhook from the same alert event.
